subject: Reparameterisation of multivariate normal with unknown parameters and observed data

messages.author: 4d57bd51ac99bdb9
messages.subject: Reparameterisation of multivariate normal with unknown parameters and observed data
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to reparameterise various MVNs in the model below for efficiency, following stan-reference-2.9.0, p. 218f.
For now I have attempted this just for one MVN. If someone could have a look whether I did this right - that'd be great.
In particular I'm unsure whether I need to increment the log probability in this particular case - and, if so, how to do it.
Please see line marked by '???' in the code below.

I also realise that the Wishart priors might not be the most efficient choice - and I would try and get onto this next.

Any other pointers on how to optimise this code would be much appreciated.

Thanks!
Tobias

// MIXING MODEL, FULL BAYES, WITH COVARIANCES
// reparameterisation after stan-reference-2.9.0, p. 218f
data {
  int J; // number of fingerprints
  int kres; // wishart parameter for residual error
  int kS; // wishart parameter for source variation
  int kZ; // wishart parameter for instrument error
  int K; // number of sources
  int N; // number of timesteps
  int Ns[K]; // numbers of source samples
  int Nz; // number of lab replicates
  vector[J] muSpriormu; // prior mu of source means
  vector[J] Ys[max(Ns),K]; // source samples
  vector[J] Yz[Nz]; // lab replicates
  vector[J] Y[N]; // target samples
  matrix[K,K-1] tV; // matrix used in ILR-transform
  cov_matrix[J] muSpriorSigma; // prior Sigma of source means
  cov_matrix[J] Rres; // wishart parameter for residual error
  cov_matrix[J] RS; // wishart parameter for source variation
  cov_matrix[J] RZ; // wishart parameter for instrument error
}

parameters {
  vector[K-1] muphi; // prior mean of ILR-transformed proportions
  vector<lower=0>[J] muS[K]; // source means
  vector[K-1] phi[N]; // ILR-transformed source proportions
  vector<lower=0>[K-1] sigma2phi; // prior variance of ILR-transformed proportions
  matrix<lower=0>[J,K] s[N]; // sources
  cov_matrix[J] Sigmares; // residual error
  cov_matrix[J] SigmaS[K]; // source variations
  cov_matrix[J] SigmaZ; // instrument error
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[K] expphiV[N]; // intermediate variable in ILR-transform
  vector<lower=0>[J] mu[N]; // target predictions
  vector[J] muZ; // lab replicate mean
  vector[K] phiV[N]; // intermediate variable in ILR-transform
  vector[J] alpha[N]; // parameter of Y reparameterisation
  matrix[J,J] L; // Cholesky decomposition of Y covariance
  simplex[K] p[N]; // source proportions

  // Prior on muZ
  for(j in 1:J) {
    muZ[j] <- 0;
  }

  // p
  for(i in 1:N) {
    phiV[i] <- tV * phi[i];
    expphiV[i] <- exp(phiV[i]);
    p[i] <- expphiV[i] / sum(expphiV[i]);
  }

  // Cholesky decomposition of Y covariance
  L <- cholesky_decompose(Sigmares+SigmaZ);

  for(i in 1:N) {
    // model equation
    mu[i] <- s[i] * p[i];
    // reparameterisation of Y likelihood
    // ??? does this require incrementing the log probability ???
    alpha[i] <- inverse(L) * (Y[i] - mu[i]);
  }
}

model {
  // hyperparameters for phi prior
  muphi ~ normal(0,1);
  sigma2phi ~ inv_gamma(2,1);

  // phi
  for(i in 1:N) {
    for (k in 1:(K-1)) {
      phi[i,k] ~ normal(muphi[k],sqrt(sigma2phi[k]));
    }
  }

  // Prior on Sigmares
  Sigmares ~ inv_wishart(kres,Rres);

  // Prior on SigmaZ
  SigmaZ ~ inv_wishart(kZ,RZ);

  // Prior on muS and SigmaS
  for(k in 1:K) {
    // ... reparameterise ...
    muS[k] ~ multi_normal(muSpriormu,muSpriorSigma);
    SigmaS[k] ~ inv_wishart(kS,RS);
  }

  // s
  for(i in 1:N) {
    for(k in 1:K) {
      // ... reparameterise ...
      s[i,,k] ~ multi_normal(muS[k],SigmaS[k]);
    }
  }

  // target data likelihood
  for(i in 1:N) {
    alpha[i] ~ normal(0,1);
    // implies: Y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i],Sigmares+SigmaZ);
  }

  // lab replicates likelihood
  for(iz in 1:Nz) {
    // ... reparameterise ...
    Yz[iz] ~ multi_normal(muZ,SigmaZ);
  }

  // source data likelihood
  for(k in 1:K) {
    for(iss in 1:Ns[k]) {
      // ... reparameterise ...
      Ys[iss,k,] ~ multi_normal(muS[k],SigmaS[k]+SigmaZ);
    }
  }
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Reparameterisation of multivariate normal with unknown parameters and observed data
parts:
No, you don't need a Jacobian adjustment when you transform
parameters and use them as parameters (rather than as variables).
For example:

parameters {
real<lower=0> alpha;
transformed parameters {
real<lower=0> inv_alpha;
inv_alpha = 1 / alpha;
model {
y ~ bar(inv_alpha); // no Jacobian needed
inv_alpha ~ foo(theta); // require log Jacobian of 1/alpha transform

Numerically, you almost never want to apply inv(Sigma) to
a matrix. And you never ever want to do

inv(a) * b

Instead, the above should be written as

a \ b

It's more efficient and more stable numerically. We're going to
start trying to add automatic warnings to this effect to the parser
in the future.

- Bob

parts:
Dear Bob,
many thanks for your help!

I thought I was using the transformed quantity (alpha) as a "variable":

First, in the transformed parameters block, I transform

alpha[i] <- L \ (Y[i] - mu[i]); (thanks for the left division note!)

with L being the Cholesky decomposition of a covariance matrix (which is an unknown parameter ("variable") itself),
Y being my observations of the modelled process (data),
mu being the results of my "deterministic" part of the model (which again involves various unknown parameters ("variables") that are sampled).

Second, in the model block, I do

alpha[i] ~ normal(0,1);

Before this reparameterisation I was doing

This last part is the MVN I'm trying to reparameterise. More details in full code below.

From what you say, I guess I would need a Jacobian adjustment - right? But I'm not sure how (if) this can actually be done in such a complicated case where various elements of the transform are unknown parameters ("variables") or data.

Any help would be much appreciated!
Tobias
